course.title: Carpentry and Furniture Making
course.tagline: Build tables, chairs and shelves with wood, tools and clean joints.

days.title: Wood, Tools and Safety
days.goal: Know the main wood types and the safety rules for every tool.

video.title: What Kind of Wood Should You Build With? | WOODWORKING BASICS

steps: Lay out a saw, hammer, tape measure, square, drill and sandpaper and name each one.
Feel pine, plywood and hardwood and note which is soft, light or heavy.
Put on safety glasses and learn the rule: never cut toward your body.
Sweep your work area and set up a steady bench or table.
days.task: Make a tool list with the job each tool does.
days.challenge: Name every tool on your bench without looking at the list.

quiz.q: What should you do first when you pick up a saw?
options: Cut as fast as you can
Check the area is clear, wear safety glasses and clamp the wood
quiz.explain: Safety comes first: glasses on, wood clamped, hands clear of the blade.

quiz.q: Which wood is soft and easy for a beginner to cut?
quiz.explain: Pine is soft, light and cheap, so it is the best wood to learn on.

quiz.q: What does the grain of wood mean?
options: The direction the wood fibres run
quiz.explain: Grain is the direction of the fibres; you cut and sand along it.

days.title: Measure and Mark Like a Pro
days.goal: Measure twice and mark wood so your cuts come out right.

video.title: What Kind of Wood Should You Build With? | WOODWORKING BASICS

steps: Measure a board three times and write the number down each time.
Mark a cut line with a pencil and a square so the line is straight.
Mark an X on the waste side so you cut on the right side of the line.
Measure a diagonal across a rectangle to check it is square.
days.task: Mark and cut a board to exactly 30cm long.
days.challenge: Cut three boards to the same length with no gaps between them.

quiz.q: How many times should you measure a board?
options: Three times, writing the number down each time
quiz.explain: Measure a board three times and write the number down each time.

quiz.q: How do you mark a straight cut line?
options: With a pencil and a square
quiz.explain: Mark a cut line with a pencil and a square so the line is straight.

quiz.q: What does the X on the board mean?
options: The waste side, so you cut on the right side of the line
quiz.explain: Mark an X on the waste side so you cut on the right side of the line. Measure a diagonal across a rectangle to check it is square.

days.title: Sawing Straight by Hand
days.goal: Cut wood straight with a hand saw.

video.title: What Kind of Wood Should You Build With? | WOODWORKING BASICS

steps: Clamp the board firmly so it cannot move.
Start the cut with short gentle pulls, then use long smooth strokes.
Watch the line, not the blade, and keep the saw straight.
Sand the cut edge smooth with sandpaper.
days.task: Cut a board straight along a marked line with no wobble.
days.challenge: Cut a board so straight it needs no sanding.

quiz.q: What should you do before you start sawing?
options: Clamp the board firmly so it cannot move
Saw as fast as you can
quiz.explain: Clamp the board firmly so it cannot move.

quiz.q: How should you start the cut?
options: With short gentle pulls, then long smooth strokes
quiz.explain: Start the cut with short gentle pulls, then use long smooth strokes.

quiz.q: What should you watch while sawing?
quiz.explain: Watch the line, not the blade, and keep the saw straight. Sand the cut edge smooth with sandpaper.

days.title: Pocket-Hole Joints Made Easy
days.goal: Join two boards with a pocket hole, a strong hidden screw joint.

video.title: Beginner's Guide to Pocket Hole Joinery

steps: A pocket hole is a hole drilled at an angle so a screw can join two boards.
Clamp the pocket-hole jig (a guide that holds the drill at the right angle) to the board.
Drill the pocket holes, then drive screws through them into the second board.
Check the joint is tight and the screw heads sit hidden inside the holes.
days.task: Join two boards at a right angle with pocket holes.
days.challenge: Join two boards so the joint holds when you lift it by one end.

quiz.q: What is a pocket hole?
options: A hole drilled at an angle so a screw can join two boards
quiz.explain: A pocket hole lets a screw pull two boards together from a hidden angle.

quiz.q: Why use pocket holes?
options: They hide the screws and make a strong joint
quiz.explain: Pocket-hole screws sit inside the hole, so the joint is strong and the screws stay hidden.

quiz.q: What does the pocket-hole jig do?
options: It holds the drill at the right angle
quiz.explain: The jig is a guide that keeps the drill bit at the correct angle for the pocket hole.

days.title: Drilling Clean Holes
days.goal: Drill straight, clean holes without splitting the wood.

video.title: Beginner's Guide to Pocket Hole Joinery

steps: Mark the hole spot with a pencil cross.
Start the drill slowly so the bit does not wander.
Drill straight down and pull the bit out often to clear the dust.
Put a scrap board underneath so the back does not split.
days.task: Drill six clean holes in a row with no splitting.
days.challenge: Drill a hole exactly where you marked it, first try.

quiz.q: How do you mark where to drill?
options: You do not need to mark it
quiz.explain: Mark the hole spot with a pencil cross.

quiz.q: Why start the drill slowly?
options: So the bit does not wander
quiz.explain: Start the drill slowly so the bit does not wander.

quiz.q: Why put a scrap board underneath?
options: So the back of the wood does not split
quiz.explain: Put a scrap board underneath so the back does not split. Pull the bit out often to clear the dust.

days.title: Screws, Glue and Clamps
days.goal: Hold wood together with screws, glue and clamps the right way.

video.title: Beginner's Guide to Pocket Hole Joinery

steps: Spread a thin even layer of wood glue on one joining face.
Press the boards together and wipe off glue that squeezes out.
Add screws while the glue is wet, then clamp the joint tight.
Leave the clamp on until the glue dries fully.
days.task: Glue and screw two boards together and test the joint the next day.
days.challenge: Glue a joint with no glue mess on the outside.

quiz.q: How much glue should you spread on a joint?
quiz.explain: Spread a thin even layer of wood glue on one joining face.

quiz.q: When do you add the screws?
options: While the glue is wet, then clamp the joint tight
quiz.explain: Add screws while the glue is wet, then clamp the joint tight.

quiz.q: When can you take the clamp off?
options: When the glue has dried fully
quiz.explain: Leave the clamp on until the glue dries fully. Wipe off glue that squeezes out.

days.title: Project: Build a Small Wooden Box
days.goal: Build a small open wooden box with glued and screwed joints.

video.title: Wood Joinery Basics

steps: Cut four sides and a bottom from one board.
Glue and screw the sides into a rectangle, checking the corners are square.
Fix the bottom on with screws from underneath.
Sand every edge smooth and check the box sits flat.
days.task: Finish a small wooden box that sits flat and holds its shape.
days.challenge: Build the box with all four corners perfectly square.

quiz.q: What parts do you cut for the small box?
quiz.explain: Cut four sides and a bottom from one board.

quiz.q: How do you fix the bottom on?
quiz.explain: Fix the bottom on with screws from underneath.

quiz.q: What should you check when the box is done?
options: That it sits flat and every edge is smooth
quiz.explain: Sand every edge smooth and check the box sits flat.

project.title: Build a Small Wooden Box
project.brief: Build a small open box with glued and screwed joints, sanded smooth.

days.title: Sanding Smooth
days.goal: Sand wood through the grits until it feels smooth.

video.title: Wood Joinery Basics

steps: Sandpaper grit is the roughness number: low numbers are rough, high numbers are fine.
Start with rough 80-grit paper, then 120, then 220.
Sand with the grain (the direction the wood lines run), never across it.
Wipe the dust off with a cloth and feel the surface with your hand.
days.task: Sand one board smooth enough to run your hand over with no roughness.
days.challenge: Sand a box inside and out with no rough spots left.

quiz.q: What does sandpaper grit mean?
options: The roughness number: low numbers are rough, high numbers are fine
quiz.explain: Sandpaper grit is the roughness number: low numbers are rough, high numbers are fine.

quiz.q: Which grits do you use, in order?
quiz.explain: Start with rough 80-grit paper, then 120, then 220.

quiz.q: Which way should you sand?
options: With the grain, never across it
quiz.explain: Sand with the grain (the direction the wood lines run), never across it.

days.title: Joints: Butt, Lap and Mitre
days.goal: Make three basic joints and know when to use each one.

video.title: Wood Joinery Basics

steps: A butt joint is two boards pushed end to face; glue and screw it.
A lap joint overlaps two boards halfway; cut a notch in each one.
A mitre joint joins two boards cut at 45 degrees, like a picture frame.
Glue all three joints and test which one is strongest.
days.task: Make one of each joint and label them.
days.challenge: Make a mitre joint with no gap at the corner.

quiz.q: What is a butt joint?
options: Two boards pushed end to face and fixed
Two boards glued edge to edge
quiz.explain: A butt joint is two boards pushed end to face; glue and screw it.

quiz.q: What is a lap joint?
options: Two boards overlapped halfway with a notch cut in each
Two boards pushed end to face
quiz.explain: A lap joint overlaps two boards halfway; cut a notch in each one.

quiz.q: What is a mitre joint?
options: Two boards cut at 45 degrees, like a picture frame
quiz.explain: A mitre joint joins two boards cut at 45 degrees, like a picture frame.

days.title: Plan an End Table
days.goal: Draw a simple plan for a small end table with measurements.

video.title: How to Build an Easy End Table

steps: Sketch the table from the front and the side.
Write the length, width and height of every part.
List the boards you need and how many of each.
Check the height works next to a real chair or sofa.
days.task: Draw a measured plan for an end table.
days.challenge: Plan a table using only boards you already have.

quiz.q: What should you sketch for the end table plan?
options: The table from the front and the side
quiz.explain: Sketch the table from the front and the side.

quiz.q: What sizes should you write on the plan?
options: The length, width and height of every part
quiz.explain: Write the length, width and height of every part.

quiz.q: What should you check about the table height?
options: That it works next to a real chair or sofa
That it is as tall as you
quiz.explain: Check the height works next to a real chair or sofa. List the boards you need and how many of each.

days.title: Cut the Table Parts
days.goal: Cut all the parts for your end table accurately.

video.title: How to Build an Easy End Table

steps: Cut the four legs to the same length first.
Cut the top, apron and shelf pieces from your plan.
Label every piece with its name and pencil marks.
Lay all the parts out on the floor like the finished table.
days.task: Cut every part for the end table, labelled and ready.
days.challenge: Cut all four legs exactly the same length.

quiz.q: What should you cut first for the table?
options: The four legs, all the same length
quiz.explain: Cut the four legs to the same length first.

quiz.q: What should you write on every piece?
quiz.explain: Label every piece with its name and pencil marks.

quiz.q: What should you do after cutting all the parts?
options: Lay them out on the floor like the finished table
quiz.explain: Lay all the parts out on the floor like the finished table.

days.title: Assemble the End Table
days.goal: Join the table parts into a steady, level table.

video.title: How to Build an Easy End Table

steps: Join the legs to the apron (the frame under the top) with pocket holes or screws.
Check the frame is square by measuring both diagonals.
Fix the top on with screws from underneath.
Stand the table up and check it does not wobble.
days.task: Assemble an end table that stands level and steady.
days.challenge: Fix a wobbly table by trimming one leg.

quiz.q: How do you join the legs to the apron?
quiz.explain: Join the legs to the apron (the frame under the top) with pocket holes or screws.

quiz.q: How do you check the frame is square?
options: Look at it from far away
quiz.explain: Check the frame is square by measuring both diagonals.

quiz.q: How do you fix the top on?
quiz.explain: Fix the top on with screws from underneath. Stand the table up and check it does not wobble.

days.title: Small Boxes: Measure Twice
days.goal: Plan a small lidded box with careful measurements.

video.title: Woodworking Basics for Beginners: Make a Beautiful Wooden Jewelry Box from Wood Scrap

steps: Decide what the box will hold and measure that item first.
Draw the box with its lid and write every size.
Choose thin boards so the box is light, not heavy.
List the hinges and screws you need for the lid.
days.task: Draw a measured plan for a lidded box.
days.challenge: Plan a box that fits a phone, keys and wallet exactly.

quiz.q: What should you measure first when planning a small box?
options: The item the box will hold
quiz.explain: Decide what the box will hold and measure that item first.

quiz.q: Why choose thin boards for a small box?
options: So the box is light, not heavy
quiz.explain: Choose thin boards so the box is light, not heavy.

quiz.q: What should you list for the lid?
options: The hinges and screws you need
quiz.explain: Draw the box with its lid and write every size. List the hinges and screws you need for the lid.

days.title: Project: Build a Small Box with a Lid
days.goal: Build a small wooden box with a hinged lid.

video.title: Woodworking Basics for Beginners: Make a Beautiful Wooden Jewelry Box from Wood Scrap

steps: Cut the sides, bottom and lid from thin boards.
Join the sides with glue and small screws or nails.
Fit two small hinges to the lid and the back.
Sand the box inside and out and test the lid opens and closes.
days.task: Finish a lidded box that opens and closes smoothly.
days.challenge: Fit hinges so the lid sits flat when closed.

quiz.q: How do you join the sides of the lidded box?
options: With glue and small screws or nails
quiz.explain: Join the sides with glue and small screws or nails.

quiz.q: How many hinges does the lid need?
quiz.explain: Fit two small hinges to the lid and the back.

quiz.q: What should you test when the box is done?
options: That the lid opens and closes well
quiz.explain: Sand the box inside and out and test the lid opens and closes.

project.title: Build a Small Box with a Lid
project.brief: Build a lidded box with hinges that open and close smoothly.

days.title: Hinges and Lids
days.goal: Fit hinges so a lid or door opens straight and stays shut.

video.title: Woodworking Basics for Beginners: Make a Beautiful Wooden Jewelry Box from Wood Scrap

steps: Mark the hinge spots on the lid and the box.
Chisel or cut a shallow recess (a flat dip) so the hinge sits flush.
Screw the hinge leaves in place, one side at a time.
Test the lid and adjust the screws if it sticks.
days.task: Fit a pair of hinges that open and close without sticking.
days.challenge: Fit a hinge so you cannot see it when the lid is closed.

quiz.q: Why cut a shallow recess for a hinge?
options: So the hinge sits flush with the wood
quiz.explain: Chisel or cut a shallow recess (a flat dip) so the hinge sits flush.

quiz.q: How should you screw the hinge in?
quiz.explain: Screw the hinge leaves in place, one side at a time.

quiz.q: What should you do if the lid sticks?
quiz.explain: Test the lid and adjust the screws if it sticks.

days.title: Build with 2x4 Timber
days.goal: Use cheap 2x4 timber (thick square-edged boards) for strong simple builds.

video.title: Three Easy 2x4 Projects For Beginners

steps: Pick straight 2x4 boards with no big bends or twists.
Cut the boards to length for a simple shelf or rack.
Join them with pocket holes or screws.
Sand the edges so no one gets splinters.
days.task: Build one small item from 2x4 timber.
days.challenge: Pick the straightest boards from a pile of ten.

quiz.q: What does 2x4 mean?
options: A board about 2 inches by 4 inches
quiz.explain: 2x4 is the size name for a common thick board, about 2 by 4 inches.

quiz.q: Why are 2x4 projects good for beginners?
options: The wood is cheap, strong and easy to cut and join
quiz.explain: 2x4 timber is cheap and forgiving, so beginners can build real furniture with it.

quiz.q: What should you check before buying 2x4 boards?
options: That the boards are straight with no big bends
quiz.explain: Bent or twisted boards make wobbly furniture, so pick straight ones.

days.title: A Simple Display Shelf
days.goal: Build a small wall shelf from 2x4 offcuts.

video.title: Three Easy 2x4 Projects For Beginners

steps: Cut two side pieces and three shelves to the same length.
Join the shelves between the sides with screws.
Check the shelf is square before the glue dries.
Sand it and hang it level on a wall.
days.task: Build and hang a small display shelf.
days.challenge: Hang the shelf perfectly level first try.

quiz.q: What pieces do you cut for the display shelf?
options: Two side pieces and three shelves
quiz.explain: Cut two side pieces and three shelves to the same length.

quiz.q: When should you check the shelf is square?
options: After it is on the wall
quiz.explain: Check the shelf is square before the glue dries.

quiz.q: How should you hang the shelf?
quiz.explain: Sand it and hang it level on a wall.

days.title: A Wall Storage Rack
days.goal: Build a rack that holds things on a wall and keeps them tidy.

video.title: Three Easy 2x4 Projects For Beginners

steps: Measure the space on the wall and the items the rack will hold.
Cut uprights and cross pieces to size.
Join the frame, then add hooks or pegs.
Fix the rack to the wall with strong screws and plugs.
days.task: Build and fix a wall storage rack.
days.challenge: Build a rack that holds 10kg without pulling off the wall.

quiz.q: What should you measure first for a wall rack?
options: The space on the wall and the items it will hold
quiz.explain: Measure the space on the wall and the items the rack will hold.

quiz.q: What do you add to the frame?
quiz.explain: Join the frame, then add hooks or pegs.

quiz.q: How do you fix the rack to the wall?
quiz.explain: Fix the rack to the wall with strong screws and plugs.

days.title: Plan a Storage Crate
days.goal: Plan a wooden crate from a single board.

video.title: Wooden Crate From A Single Board

steps: Draw the crate with its slats and handles.
Work out how many pieces you can cut from one board.
Mark the handle holes on the side panels.
List the glue, nails and sandpaper you need.
days.task: Draw a plan for a crate that uses one board only.
days.challenge: Plan a crate that holds books without the bottom sagging.

quiz.q: What should you draw for the crate plan?
options: The crate with its slats and handles
quiz.explain: Draw the crate with its slats and handles.

quiz.q: What should you work out from one board?
options: How many pieces you can cut from it
quiz.explain: Work out how many pieces you can cut from one board.

quiz.q: What should you mark on the side panels?
quiz.explain: Mark the handle holes on the side panels. List the glue, nails and sandpaper you need.

days.title: Cut and Glue the Crate Panels
days.goal: Cut crate panels and glue them into flat sides.

video.title: Wooden Crate From A Single Board

steps: Cut the board into equal lengths for the sides.
Glue two pieces edge to edge for each side panel and clamp them.
Leave the glue to dry overnight before you cut further.
Trim the glued panels square.
days.task: Glue up two flat side panels for the crate.
days.challenge: Glue a panel with no gaps between the boards.

quiz.q: How do you make one side panel?
options: Glue two pieces edge to edge and clamp them
Nail pieces on top of each other
quiz.explain: Glue two pieces edge to edge for each side panel and clamp them.

quiz.q: How long should the glued panels dry?
quiz.explain: Leave the glue to dry overnight before you cut further.

quiz.q: What should you do after the panels dry?
quiz.explain: Trim the glued panels square.

days.title: Project: Build a Wooden Storage Crate
days.goal: Assemble the crate with slats, handles and a strong base.

video.title: Wooden Crate From A Single Board

steps: Cut the slats and side panels to your plan.
Join the sides to the base with glue and nails.
Cut handle holes in the side panels and round the edges.
Sand the whole crate and test it carries a full load of books.
days.task: Finish a wooden crate that carries books without bending.
days.challenge: Build the crate using only one board, as planned.

quiz.q: How do you join the crate sides to the base?
quiz.explain: Join the sides to the base with glue and nails.

quiz.q: What should you do to the handle holes?
options: Cut them and round the edges
quiz.explain: Cut handle holes in the side panels and round the edges.

quiz.q: How do you test the finished crate?
options: Check it carries a full load of books
quiz.explain: Sand the whole crate and test it carries a full load of books.

project.title: Build a Wooden Storage Crate
project.brief: Build a crate with slats, handles and a strong base from one board.
checks: Made from one board as planned

days.title: Stools: Legs and Angles
days.goal: Understand splayed legs (legs that angle outward) and why they make stools steady.

video.title: I Built a Wooden Stool — Easy DIY Anyone Can Make

steps: Cut a leg at an 8-degree angle and see how it leans.
Mark the same angle on all four legs.
Dry-fit the legs to the top without glue to check the angles.
Learn why angled legs stop a stool tipping over.
days.task: Cut four legs with matching angles.
days.challenge: Explain to a friend why splayed legs are steadier.

quiz.q: What are splayed legs?
options: Legs that angle outward from the top
quiz.explain: Splayed legs are legs that angle outward.

quiz.q: What angle do you cut the stool legs at?
quiz.explain: Cut a leg at an 8-degree angle and see how it leans. Mark the same angle on all four legs.

quiz.q: Why do angled legs make a stool steady?
options: They stop the stool tipping over
quiz.explain: Learn why angled legs stop a stool tipping over. Dry-fit the legs to the top without glue to check the angles.

days.title: Build a Wooden Stool
days.goal: Build a sturdy wooden stool with splayed legs.

video.title: I Built a Wooden Stool — Easy DIY Anyone Can Make

steps: Cut the legs, top and corner blocks from your plan.
Fix the legs to the corner blocks under the top.
Add stretchers (bars between the legs) to stop wobble.
Sand, stain or oil the stool and test it by sitting on it.
days.task: Build a stool you can sit on safely.
days.challenge: Build a stool that does not wobble on a flat floor.

quiz.q: What holds the stool legs under the top?
quiz.explain: Fix the legs to the corner blocks under the top.

quiz.q: What are stretchers on a stool?
options: Bars between the legs that stop wobble
quiz.explain: Add stretchers (bars between the legs) to stop wobble.

quiz.q: How do you test the finished stool?
quiz.explain: Sand, stain or oil the stool and test it by sitting on it.

days.title: Stretchers and Strength
days.goal: Add stretchers and check a stool or table for strength.

video.title: I Built a Wooden Stool — Easy DIY Anyone Can Make

steps: Measure the gaps between the legs for the stretcher bars.
Cut stretchers to fit snugly between the legs.
Glue and screw them in place.
Rock the stool hard and check nothing moves.
days.task: Fit stretchers that make a stool rock-solid.
days.challenge: Fix a wobbly stool by adding one stretcher.

quiz.q: What should you measure for the stretcher bars?
quiz.explain: Measure the gaps between the legs for the stretcher bars.

quiz.q: How should the stretchers fit?
quiz.explain: Cut stretchers to fit snugly between the legs. Glue and screw them in place.

quiz.q: How do you test the stool's strength?
options: Rock it hard and check nothing moves
quiz.explain: Rock the stool hard and check nothing moves.

days.title: Plan a Dining Table
days.goal: Plan a dining table: top, legs and apron, with real measurements.

video.title: How to Build a DIY Dining Table

steps: Measure the space and decide how many people it must seat.
Draw the top, legs and apron with sizes.
Choose boards wide enough for the top.
Work out the cost of the wood before you buy.
days.task: Draw a measured plan for a dining table.
days.challenge: Plan a table that seats six in a small room.

quiz.q: What should you decide first when planning a dining table?
options: How many people it must seat
quiz.explain: Measure the space and decide how many people it must seat.

quiz.q: What parts should your drawing show with sizes?
quiz.explain: Draw the top, legs and apron with sizes.

quiz.q: What should you work out before you buy the wood?
quiz.explain: Choose boards wide enough for the top. Work out the cost of the wood before you buy.

days.title: Tabletop and Legs
days.goal: Join boards into a wide tabletop and fix strong legs.

video.title: How to Build a DIY Dining Table

steps: Glue boards edge to edge for the top and clamp them flat.
Leave the top to dry overnight, then sand it flat.
Fix the legs to the apron frame with strong joints.
Join the top to the frame with screws from below.
days.task: Join a tabletop with no gaps between boards.
days.challenge: Make a tabletop flat enough that a glass does not rock.

quiz.q: How do you join boards into a wide tabletop?
options: Nail them on top of each other
Glue them edge to edge and clamp them flat
Screw them to the legs only
quiz.explain: Edge-gluing boards side by side makes one wide flat top.

quiz.q: Why clamp a tabletop while the glue dries?
options: To hold the boards flat and tight so the top has no gaps
quiz.explain: Clamps press the boards together and keep them flat while the glue sets.

quiz.q: Why screw the top on from underneath?
options: So no screw heads show on the top surface
quiz.explain: Screws from below keep the tabletop smooth and clean on top.

days.title: Finish a Tabletop
days.goal: Stain and seal a tabletop so it looks good and resists spills.

video.title: How to Build a DIY Dining Table

steps: Sand the top smooth up to 220-grit paper.
Wipe on stain evenly and let it dry.
Brush or wipe on a clear sealer in thin coats.
Sand lightly between coats and add a second coat.
days.task: Finish a tabletop with an even stain and smooth sealer.
days.challenge: Fix a patchy stain by sanding back and starting again.

quiz.q: How smooth should you sand a tabletop before staining?
quiz.explain: Sand the top smooth up to 220-grit paper.

quiz.q: How should you put the sealer on?
quiz.explain: Brush or wipe on a clear sealer in thin coats.

quiz.q: What should you do between coats of sealer?
options: Sand lightly and add a second coat
quiz.explain: Sand lightly between coats and add a second coat.

days.title: Farmhouse Style Basics
days.goal: Know the farmhouse look: chunky legs, wide planks and a warm finish.

video.title: How to Build a Farmhouse Kitchen Table

steps: Look at farmhouse tables and note the thick legs and wide top.
Choose a warm stain colour that suits the style.
Learn how an apron under the top adds strength and looks.
Sketch your own farmhouse table.
days.task: Sketch a farmhouse table with labels for each part.
days.challenge: Name three things that make a table look farmhouse style.

quiz.q: What makes a table look farmhouse style?
options: Chunky legs, wide planks and a warm finish
quiz.explain: The farmhouse look is chunky legs, wide planks and a warm finish.

quiz.q: What does the apron do on a farmhouse table?
options: It adds strength and looks good
quiz.explain: An apron under the top adds strength and looks.

quiz.q: What kind of stain suits the farmhouse style?

days.title: Capstone Planning

capstone.title: Build a Small Table or Shelf for a Real Home
capstone.brief: Design and build a small table or shelf for a real room in a home, finished, level and strong, and present it with a costing sheet.
checks: Piece designed from real measurements of the room
Piece stands level with no wobble
Sanded smooth with no splinters or rough spots
Finish even: stain or sealer applied neatly
Costing sheet shows wood, screws, glue, time and selling price
deliverables: Finished table or shelf, level and strong
Four photos: front, side, back and top
